column4: What is a cool activity you've done on a vacation?
column5:
I'm not really sure I've done anything “cool” on a vacation. Does that reflect poorly on me? Almost surely. In any case, this is something that did happen on a vacation.

A bit over a decade ago, I went on a family vacation to Istanbul. On the first day—this was in the early days of Uber—I went out on my own and booked an Uber way up the Bosphorus to the headquarters of a large Turkish company (that manufactures steel pipes and imports BMWs) that opens its building to the public over the weekend as a contemporary art gallery. It was an odd setting in which to see art—you walk around these conference rooms with Polycoms, and you look up there's art by artists whose names you'd recognize on the wall. They had a traveling show from SFMOMA at the time, I recall. Anyway, I have a fun time, the sun is setting over the Bosphorus, it's time to go home... and I can't hail an Uber. This was, as I mentioned, the early days of Uber, and also I was an hour or two outside the city center. Also my phone's about to die. So I stumble around until I happen upon a taxi. The whole ride back (two hours with traffic!) the taxi driver, who doesn't speak English, keeps trying to talk to me. And there's this one thing he keeps repeating, emphatically. About half-way home, he pulls over and calls someone off the street to translate into English. It turns out this whole time he was trying to invite me to have tea with him! Which is very nice. But my phone was about to die, we were still an hour away from my hotel, and I was exhausted. So I thanked him profusely and apologized and requested that we continue on to my hotel. At one point, as we get closer to the city center, he takes a turn into oncoming traffic. Horns blare. He looks back sheepishly, and pointing to his head gives me the universal “coo-coo” gesture (which, I guess, transcends cultural and language boundaries). Despite claiming that he did, he definitely didn't know where my hotel was, so in my phone's last moments of battery life, I just started giving right-turn/left-turn hand signals for every turn. Finally made it home. And then I woke up with a terrible sinus infection and was bedridden for the rest of my time in Istanbul. Would love to return one day and the city beyond a single corporate headquarters!
column6: What is the best concert you've ever been to?
column7:
Two contenders:
1) LA, 2012, Philip Glass's opera “Einstein of the Beach” (one of the last performances with the original creative team). One of the most beautiful pieces of art ever created. After sitting in a chair for four-and-a-half hours, the catharsis I felt when “Knee Play 5” starts and the narrator intones, “TWO LOVERS SAT ON A PARK BENCH WITH THEIR BODIES TOUCHING EACH OTHER HOLDING HANDS IN THE MOONLIGHT”... man, it fucking got me, totally misty-eyed.

2) Also that same year, 2012! On my twenty-first birthday, I was at an LA Phil concert at the Hollywood Bowl, and I thought, hey, on the way back maybe I'll stop by a bar. Hollywood is a garbage neighborhood but there was one bar that was highly-rated on Google Maps, so I headed there. I walked in to this cramped dive bar to find someone playing some insane jazz piano. So, so good. I got a drink (a French 75, which I mention just so you can join me in making fun of younger me). The pianist finishes his set, and another band comes on, and they're even better than the pianist! They absolutely play the doors off the venue. Not a single body in the extremely-cramped venue is still, everyone is dancing. I thought, this place is sick!!! And there's no cover?? So every couple of weeks I come back, because they play every Wednesday. A few months later Kendrick Lamar's “To Pimp a Butterfly” comes out, and I hear all this buzz about the bandleader on the album being the next big thing in jazz. Turns out this whole time I was hearing Kamasi Washington and his crew (The West Coast Get Down)!
